observed.facings.png: Three facings of a small two-legged reptile on a checkerboard at one scale. South is a compact, upright animal facing the camera with a short tail stub poking out at the left. East is a long, low, slender theropod with its body and tail horizontal. North is a narrow upright rear view with the tail hanging between the legs. South and north stand visibly taller than east.
observed.south.png: Front view: a broad, flat-topped lizard head with two dark side-set eyes under angry brow ridges, small nostrils, and a wide mouth line curling up at the ends like a slight smile. Pale tan chest and belly, two tiny forelimbs held in front, two sturdy legs with toed feet. Olive netted scales on flanks and crown only, with low knobs on top of the head instead of a clear crest. The head sits high above an upright torso.
observed.east.png: True side profile of a small theropod: horizontal body, long thick tapering tail straight back, tiny forelimbs under the chest, two hind legs with reddish-pink shins and feet. The head is small to moderate, about a fifth of total length, with a tapering beak-like snout, one dark eye, spiky jowls and a backswept horn crest. The hide is an even olive net with pale tan lines; the belly is tan.
observed.north.png: Rear view: back of the head with small knobs at both sides and no face or eyes, a long neck, rows of olive scales down the back, the tail hanging down the centre to a blunt tip between the legs, the backs of two legs, and small elbow bumps at the sides.
observed.scale.png: Beside the human, the east facing is a low animal well under half the human's height and more than half a cell long. At normal play it is a thin, pale tan-olive streak that nearly disappears into the brown ground, much fainter than the dark rat next to it.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face with both eyes, pale chest and belly, and forelimbs toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head, the scaled back, the tail and the backs of the legs, with no face or eyes. The side knobs are the cheek and crest ridges.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are ground-level views with the legs planted below the body.

SAME_SIZE.seen: South and north stand clearly taller than east. Part of this is pose, because the torso and neck are drawn upright in south and north and horizontal in east, but the south head and legs are also a little larger than in east.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same olive net, tan belly, forelimbs, legs and tail throughout, and the tail turns with the body. The crest is a distinct horn in east but only low knobs in south and north, and the stance is more upright in south and north; both are minor drift.

SIGNATURE.seen: The bipedal reptile stance, tiny forelimbs and thick balancing tail are all clear, and the head is reasonably blunt from the front.

ALIEN.seen: It reads as a small theropod dinosaur, which is the body plan the canon list asks for. All listed departures are present and it is not a frog or a sprawling lizard.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 two legs: present on every facing. 2 blunt head: present from the front, weaker in east where the snout tapers. 3 tiny forelimbs: present in south and east, elbows in north. 4 thick balancing tail: present, long in east, stub in south, hanging in north.

CANON.seen: Body plan: yes in east, upright torso in south and north. Head: no, not oversized in east, with a tapering snout, no broad fleshy cheeks and an upcurled mouth in south; the crest is present in east. Eyes: yes, two, modest. Colour: no, a near-uniform olive net with tan lines and no warm orange-brown patches; pale belly present. Size: yes. Realistic rendering: yes. Negative line: yes, not a frog and not four-legged.

STYLE.seen: Painterly scales, natural shading and real anatomy with thin dark edges. The south face has a mild smile line but is not toy-like.

OURS.seen: The card gives an in-house generation job as provenance, and it does not resemble a vanilla animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs with no ground, shadow or scenery. Only an extremely faint residue is noticeable around south when enlarged on grey.

SCALE.seen: Roughly knee to thigh height beside the human, so a vermin-scale animal as described.

LEGIBLE.seen: In the normal-play panel the thin tan-olive east sprite nearly blends into the brown ground and reads as a faint streak, while the rat beside it is clear.

reply.subject: RSW_Gizka
reply.image_seen: Image 1 shows three olive-and-tan reptile facings at shared scale; image 2 shows the broad-faced front with tucked arms; image 3 shows a horizontal biped with a long tapering tail; image 4 shows the rear, central tail and hind legs without eyes; image 5 shows a small creature beside a human.

concerns.evidence: The east head is modest relative to the torso, with little fleshy cheek volume behind the mouth. Its snout tip is rounded rather than sharply pointed, but the oversized, broad-cheeked head is missing. The south mouth also curves upward at its corners.

The back and flanks carry a fairly uniform olive field divided by tan scale outlines. Warm reddish brown is concentrated on the hands and lower legs; distinct warm orange-brown patches across the back, flanks and head are missing.

The measured 29% height spread is visible, but the east neck reaches forward and its hind legs are bent. Head and foot dimensions remain broadly comparable across the shared-scale panel. The height difference does not establish a change in the animal's scale.

The south torso is viewed end-on, with its tail projecting behind the left hip. North shows the back leading toward the central tapering tail between the haunches. These are compatible with a foreshortened horizontal body; neither view clearly demonstrates an upright hopper. East explicitly shows the horizontal theropod posture.

East has a distinct swept-back projection behind the crown. South and north show low crown relief, but its connection to that projection cannot be resolved confidently in these small images. A clearer rear-skull detail would distinguish foreshortening from an anatomical omission.

The south mouth corners rise slightly, but the face has modest inset eyes, irregular scales and natural shaded volume. The mouth conflicts with the specified downturned expression, already covered by K1, without clearly making the rendering cartoonish.
